subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does a controlled current-main WebSocket test show that an unauthenticated or lower-scope peer can cause an accepted request or event solely by predicting another connection's sequence number?
rationale: Source inspection indicates sequence numbers are non-authoritative ordering metadata, but the protected security report requires an owner-confirmed boundary test before dismissal or protocol changes.

options.title: Validate the boundary
options.body: Exercise raw clients with missing, invalid, low-scope, and privileged authentication and close as non-reproducible if sequence values never affect frame acceptance or session authority.

options.title: Escalate private remediation
options.body: If any unauthorized request or cross-connection injection succeeds, move the details to the private security process and fix authentication or authorization binding rather than randomizing event counters.

recommendation.title: Validate the boundary
recommendation.body: Exercise raw clients with missing, invalid, low-scope, and privileged authentication and close as non-reproducible if sequence values never affect frame acceptance or session authority.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Gateway client and SDK transport work makes this the strongest available owner signal for coordinating protocol-boundary validation.
